correctness.rationale: Exact matching uniqueness plus contraction gives a bijection between each matching-containing tree and a Cayley tree with n-1 independent fair lift coins. Path-edge transition bits yield d=2L-H-c1+cL and the exact parity-binomial law. Counting labeled Cayley paths yields the Rayleigh tail. A uniform McDiarmid bound over 4n^2 pairs combined with tight Cayley diameter proves the whole measured-metric 3/2 dilation via measure-preserving projection. Checker verify.py independently exhausts all balanced bipartite trees for n=2,3,4 and Prüfer Cayley trees through n=6 (943 exact assertions). Finite enumeration is corroboration, not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The perfect-matchability event in a uniform bipartite spanning tree is exponentially rare and natural. A full exact conditional law and a 3/2 universal metric dilation show how this rare structural constraint changes the whole random geometry. Pair-distance fluctuations and a continuum-tree limit are meaningful structural results, not an unmotivated finite invariant or routine repetition of the known counting formula.
